milestones.title: Ahmedabad founded
milestones.detail: Sultan Ahmad Shah I laid the foundation of a new walled capital on the east bank of the Sabarmati on 26 February 1411, beside the older town of Ashaval, and built the Bhadra citadel.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 5, 'Ahmadabad City', pp. 106-109, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee05grea; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad

milestones.title: Jama Masjid completed
milestones.detail: The city's great congregational mosque was finished on 4 January 1424 by Ahmad Shah I.
milestones.source: Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency, vol. IV: Ahmedabad (1879), https://archive.org/details/dli.csl.3354

milestones.title: City walls strengthened by Mahmud Begada
milestones.detail: Mahmud Begada put the walls built by Ahmad Shah into thorough repair, making Ahmedabad one of the strongest cities in India. Wikipedia dates the outer wall, about 10 km round with twelve gates, to 1487.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 5, 'Ahmadabad City', pp. 106-109, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee05grea; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad

milestones.title: Conquered by Akbar
milestones.detail: Ahmedabad and the rest of Gujarat were taken into the Mughal Empire; it remained a rich provincial capital and textile centre through the 17th century.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 5, 'Ahmadabad City', pp. 106-109, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee05grea

milestones.title: Marathas take the city
milestones.detail: After decades of fighting between Mughal and Maratha leaders the city was finally acquired by the Marathas.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 5, 'Ahmadabad City', pp. 106-109, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee05grea

milestones.title: British rule begins
milestones.detail: On the overthrow of the Peshwa the greatly depopulated city passed to the East India Company; its walls were restored in 1832.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 5, 'Ahmadabad City', pp. 106-109, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee05grea

milestones.title: Earthquake
milestones.detail: A severe earthquake in June 1819 threw down the shaking minarets of the Jama Masjid and destroyed many houses.
milestones.source: Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency, vol. IV: Ahmedabad (1879), https://archive.org/details/dli.csl.3354, p. 261

milestones.title: First cotton mill opens
milestones.detail: The Ahmedabad Cotton Mills Company opened in June 1861, the first of the steam mills that made the city a textile centre.
milestones.source: Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency, vol. IV: Ahmedabad (1879), https://archive.org/details/dli.csl.3354

milestones.title: Railway from Bombay reaches Ahmedabad
milestones.detail: The Bombay and Baroda Railway was opened as far as Ahmedabad.
milestones.source: Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency, vol. IV: Ahmedabad (1879), https://archive.org/details/dli.csl.3354

milestones.title: Sabarmati flood
milestones.detail: Floods rose over a large part of the city and damaged 3,887 houses; they also destroyed most of the first, wooden Ellis Bridge.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 5, 'Ahmadabad City', pp. 106-109, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee05grea; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellis_Bridge

milestones.title: Steel Ellis Bridge built
milestones.detail: A steel bridge across the Sabarmati replaced the wooden one, opening the west bank to the city's later growth.

milestones.title: Gandhi founds the Sabarmati Ashram
milestones.detail: Mahatma Gandhi established the Satyagraha Ashram on the bank of the Sabarmati, from which the Salt March set out in 1930.
milestones.source: Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation, History of Ahmedabad, http://www.egovamc.com/AhmCity/history.aspx, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad

milestones.title: Capital of the new state of Gujarat
milestones.detail: Ahmedabad became the state capital on 1 May 1960 when Bombay State was divided; the capital later moved to the new city of Gandhinagar.
milestones.source: Yagnik & Sheth, The Shaping of Modern Gujarat (2005), https://books.google.com/books?id=wmKIiAPgnF0C, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad

milestones.title: Gujarat earthquake
milestones.detail: The earthquake of 26 January 2001 brought down up to 50 multi-storey buildings in the city and killed 752 people there.
milestones.source: WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia, Lessons learned from the Gujarat earthquake, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad

milestones.title: Historic City of Ahmadabad inscribed by UNESCO
milestones.detail: The walled city was added to the World Heritage List.
milestones.source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1551/, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad

milestones.title: Ahmedabad Metro opens
milestones.detail: The first 6.5 km section of the east-west corridor was inaugurated on 4 March 2019.

landmarks.name: Manek Burj
landmarks.source: Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency, vol. IV: Ahmedabad (1879), https://archive.org/details/dli.csl.3354; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manek_Burj
landmarks.note: Bastion of the Bhadra citadel said to be built round the city's foundation stone; 53 ft high on the outside as measured in 1879. It was partly removed in 1999 to make space for the new road bridges beside Ellis Bridge, so the height describes the bastion as it stood before then.

landmarks.note: 25 ft is the height of the three arches as given in 1879; the parapet above is not included, so the full gateway is somewhat taller.

landmarks.name: Queen's Mosque, Mirzapur (Rani Rupamati's Mosque)
landmarks.source: Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency, vol. IV: Ahmedabad (1879), https://archive.org/details/dli.csl.3354
landmarks.note: 32 ft high. The Gazetteer dates it only to 'probably the latter years (1430-1440)' of Ahmad Shah I's reign; 1440 is the end of that range. Its minarets were broken short in the 1819 earthquake.

landmarks.name: Muhafiz Khan Mosque
landmarks.source: Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency, vol. IV: Ahmedabad (1879), https://archive.org/details/dli.csl.3354

landmarks.name: Rani Sipri's Mosque
landmarks.source: Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency, vol. IV: Ahmedabad (1879), https://archive.org/details/dli.csl.3354

landmarks.name: Patang Hotel (revolving restaurant tower)
landmarks.source: Limca Book of Records (2018), as cited at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patang_Hotel

notes: Start date: 1411 is the documented founding of Ahmedabad by Ahmad Shah I. It is contested in one respect: an older town, Ashaval (and a Chaulukya foundation called Karnavati, whose exact site is not known), stood on or beside the site from about the 11th century, so the settlement is older than the city's name. Population: figures to 1800 are Chandler's estimates; the peak of 385,000 in 1700 and the collapse to about 100,000 by 1750 are his reading of travellers' accounts and are rough (the 1908 Imperial Gazetteer repeats a tradition of 900,000, which is not used). 1817-1851 are official returns quoted in the 1879 Bombay Gazetteer; 1872-1891 are censuses as given in the Imperial Gazetteer (city with cantonment); 1901-1941 are the Census of India's back-cast series for the urban agglomeration, a wider area, so there is a break of definition between 1891 and 1901. Landmarks: heights for the old monuments come from the 1879 Bombay Gazetteer, which gives them in feet for only a few buildings. Left out for lack of a sourced height: Bhadra Fort itself, the Jama Masjid, Sidi Saiyyed Mosque, the Sidi Bashir 'shaking minarets' (a height of 69.5 ft is attributed to Archnet but the page could not be opened), Sarkhej Roza, Hutheesing Jain Temple, Ellis Bridge, Sabarmati Ashram, Narendra Modi Stadium and the Atal Bridge. Modern towers are missing entirely: the CTBUH Skyscraper Center lists no buildings for Ahmedabad, and the heights on Wikipedia's list (for example Mondeal One, 148 m) are sourced only to developers' pages that do not state them, so none is recorded. Only six landmarks could be sourced.
